title.narrative: Caribe Afirmativo: Countering violence against LGBTIQ+ people
Caribe Afirmativo: Motverka våld mot hbtqi-personer

description.narrative: Corporación Caribe Afirmativo (CA) is an organization founded in the Colombian Caribbean region, with over 15 years of experience in defending and promoting LGBTIQ+ rights in Colombia and the region, using an intersectional and territorial approach. The project aims at strengthening the capacities of civil society organizations in Latin America to address hate speech and violence against LGBTIQ+ people. This will be done through two specific objectives: - To analyze the levels of violence and discrimination faced by LGBTIQ+ individuals in the region, and to identify civil society organizations and community strategies aimed at addressing and countering this problem. - To develop a regional work strategy with civil society organizations with a community focus, aimed at reducing discrimination, hate speech, and violence against LGBTIQ+ people.

Corporación Caribe Afirmativo (CA) är en organisation grundad i den colombianska karibiska regionen, med över 15 års erfarenhet av att försvara och främja HBTQI+-personers rättigheter i Colombia och regionen, med hjälp av ett intersektionellt och territoriellt arbetssätt. Projektet syftar till att stärka kapaciteten hos civilsamhällesorganisationer i Latinamerika att motverka hatretorik och våld mot HBTQI+-personer. Detta kommer att ske genom att verka för två specifika mål: - Att analysera nivåerna av våld och diskriminering som HBTQI+-personer upplever i regionen, och att identifiera civilsamhällesorganisationer och strategier på lokal nivå som syftar till att motverka dessa problem. - Att utveckla en regional strategi för lokal verksamhet tillsammans med civilsamhällesorganisationer, vilken syftar till att minska diskriminering, hatretorik och våld mot HBTQI+-personer.

The overall objective of the contribution is to strengthen the capacities of civil society organizations in Latin America to address hate speech and violence against LGBTIQ people.
This will be done through two specific objectives:
1.To analyze the levels of violence and discrimination faced by LGBTIQ individuals in the region, and to identify civil society organizations and community strategies aimed at addressing and countering this problem.
2.To develop a regional work strategy with civil society organizations with a community focus, aimed at reducing discrimination, hate speech, and violence against LGBTIQ people.

Regarding Result 1, the project contributed to strengthening understanding of the discrimination and violence faced by LGBTIQ people across Latin America, as well as generating a solid evidence base on community level responses and the community based organizations (CBOs) working to address them. This was achieved through the following actions: •Mapping and engaging 21 CBOs across 14 countries, surpassing the initial target by five. The mapping covered Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Panama, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Peru, and Venezuela. An intersectional selection criteria was applied in this selection to ensure representation of CBOs working with youth, LBT women, Afro descendant communities, and populations in marginalized or peripheral areas. •Documenting community based initiatives focused on preventing, documenting, and responding to violence and discrimination against LGBTIQ people. An analytical report (Product 1) was produced, synthesizing methodologies, key results, lessons learned, and the main gaps and challenges affecting the impact and sustainability of community level LGBTIQ rights work. •Developing a dedicated micro website (Product 2) to ensure public access to the mapping results and other knowledge products generated under Result 1. Contents can be accessed in the following link: https://www.caribeafirmativo.lgbt/protejiendodiversidades/
Regarding Result 2, the project contributed to strengthened regional collaboration among CBOs, enhanced collective capacities, and produced practical tools to support community level action to address discrimination, hate speech, and violence against LGBTIQ people. This was accomplished through the following activities: •Organizing a regional social innovation encounter in Bogotá with representatives from 20 CBOs across 13 countries, preceded by three virtual preparatory sessions to facilitate initial exchanges and alignment. During the encounter, visibility and stakeholder engagement was increased through a reception hosted by the Swedish Ambassador to Colombia, attended by public institutions, civil society organizations, and international actors. •Facilitating peer learning and capacity strengthening, enabling participants to exchange experiences, identify complementary strengths, and deepen their understanding of community level approaches to defending LGBTIQ rights. This was documented through a shared conceptual framework for community level LGBTIQ rights work in the social innovation encounter minutes (Product 3). •Co creating the Toolbox for LGBTIQ Community Level Work (Product 4), available in Spanish and Portuguese, which provides practical guidance across six areas: dialogue and training initiatives; cultural and artistic tools for social transformation; community communication and advocacy; documentation and memory of human rights violations; advocacy and organizational sustainability; and fundraising strategies. •Creating the Regional Network of LGBTIQ Community Level Work, which represents the projects principal achievement under this result and provides a sustained platform for regional coordination among CBOs. In support of the Networks future activities, participating organizations developed a collaborative workplan for 20252026 (Product 5) outlining priorities to strengthen community level action, enhance visibility in public agendas, consolidate communication and memory strategies, promote regional articulation, and mobilize additional resources. •Implementing the #SomosMuchas (#WeAreMany) communication campaign (Product 6), which reached approximately 87,563 people across social media platforms and increased the visibility of LGBTIQ CBOs. The campaign contributed to strengthening recognition of community based initiatives, enhancing advocacy capacity, and countering discriminatory narratives in digital environments.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
